question.text: In curing cement plasters water is sprinkled from time to time. This helps in

options.text: developing interlocking needle-like crystals of hydrated silicates
hydrating sand and gravel mixed with cement

solution.text: Water develops interlocking needle-like crystals of hydrated silicates. The reactions involved are the hydration of calcium aluminates and calcium silicates which change into their colloidal gels. At the same time, some calcium hydroxide and aluminium hydroxides are formed as precipitates due to hydrolysis. Calcium hydroxide binds the particles of calcium silicates together while aluminium hydroxide fills the interstices rendering the mass impervious.
